title: The etale compact-support comparisons
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring and use bounded-below complexes of ordinary $\Lambda$-module sheaves on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a compactifiable separated finite-type morphism of Noetherian schemes [def-asd-compactifiable], where Noetherian means admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings. Restrict the chosen-compactification candidates of [def-amb-etale-compact-support] to $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$. The proper-refinement comparisons of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison] are natural coherent isomorphisms: identities and composites of refinements give identities and composites of comparisons, and comparison through a common refinement is independent of that refinement and satisfies the cocycle condition. Thus these candidates are canonically identified, denoted $Rf_!$. For composable compactifiable separated finite-type morphisms $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ of Noetherian schemes, these identifications give a natural composition isomorphism $Rg_!Rf_!\cong R(gf)_!$ on $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},\Lambda)$, independent of compactification choices and associative for three such morphisms.

proof.text: The stipulated finite affine cover witnesses local Noetherianity by [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Each affine is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so their finite union is quasi-compact (restrict an open cover to each affine and join the finite subcovers). By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], every original scheme is quasi-separated. For a compactification $X\hookrightarrow\overline X\to Y$, the proper map to the locally Noetherian base is finite type, hence its ambient scheme is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. It is in particular locally Noetherian, hence quasi-separated by the preceding lemma. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] now makes the open immersion quasi-compact since its source X is quasi-compact. We can therefore apply the qcqs compactification results. For the finite-ring bounded-below candidates, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-iso] and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison-composition] make the specified alpha maps [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison] invertible and compatible with identity and composition. For a refinement $u:e\to c$, let $A_u:F_c\to F_e$ be the result of applying the ambient proper pushforward to alpha and the canonical direct-image composition identification, where $F_c=Rf_!^c$. Using [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] and the unit and associativity calculation on bounded-below injective representatives in step 3, $A_{ut}=A_tA_u$ and $A_{\operatorname{id}}=\operatorname{id}$. By [prop-nagata-compactification-category], the category is nonempty and cofiltered, including equalization of parallel refinements without a density assumption. For $u:e\to c$ and $v:e\to d$, set $C_{c,d}=A_v^{-1}A_u$. Given a second span through $e'$, take a common refinement $z$ of $e,e'$ and then equalize the resulting parallel arrows to $c$ and to $d$ successively. On this final refinement both pairs of composites are equal. The composition formula cancels its invertible comparison factors, so the two expressions for $C_{c,d}$ agree. For three objects take one common refinement; then $C_{d,b}C_{c,d}=(A_w^{-1}A_v)(A_v^{-1}A_u)=A_w^{-1}A_u=C_{c,b}$, and $C_{c,c}=\operatorname{id}$. This proves the specified alpha comparisons give exactly the canonical identification and cocycle claimed in the first clause, on the same domain as [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-compactification-independence].

Choose a compactification $d=(v,q)$ of $g$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle] to obtain $e=(a,p)$ of $vf$, with $V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$, $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$, $p_Y:V\to Y$, and $c:X\hookrightarrow V$. It supplies the actual compactifications $(c,p_Y)$ of $f$ and $(a,qp)$ of $gf$, and $a=bc$. The candidate restriction on D+ is the same formula $Rp_*j_!$ as in its definition [def-amb-etale-compact-support].

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-open-proper-interchange] to the Cartesian square $pb=vp_Y$ and to $c_!K$. This gives $v_!Rp_{Y*}c_!K\cong Rp_*b_!c_!K$. The input remains in D+ by exact degreewise extension by zero [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact]. By [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition], the degreewise coherent isomorphism $b_!c_!\cong a_!$ descends to complexes and localization: its inverse and its identities remain inverse and identities after applying the localization functor. Applying $Rq_*$ and the comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] yields the explicit chain
$$Rg_!^dRf_!^{(c,p_Y)}=Rq_*v_!Rp_{Y*}c_!\xrightarrow{Rq_*\gamma}Rq_*Rp_*b_!c_!\cong R(qp)_*a_!=R(gf)_!^{(a,qp)}.$$
Apply the ringed-topos statement to the small etale topoi with constant coefficient ring $\Lambda$, in a universe in which these sites are small. Its canonical comparison restricts to D+ and is coherent there as follows. Enough injectives [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] and [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] give a bounded-below injective representative I. Direct image preserves injective terms [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-preserves-injectives] and zero terms, so p_*I is bounded-below K-injective. In the normalization of the ringed-topos theorem choose the resolution p_*I to be the identity: the composition comparison is then the underived identification q_*p_*I=(qp)_*I. For three maps both parenthesizations are the same underived identification on I: at an etale test object both iterated fibre products are identified with the single fibre product by the unique map preserving every projection [def-pc-fibre-product]. Identity maps give identity identifications. All are linear for the same constant ring by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Naturality and the fact that every D+ object has such a representative prove the unit and associativity laws on D+. The computation of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] also shows the lower bound is preserved. Finally conjugate this chain by the step-1 comparisons to any prescribed candidates for $f,g,gf$.

For each auxiliary triangle take the supplied compactification of $gf$ to be $(a_i,q_ip_i)$; the last clause of [lem-cbc-compactifiable-compatible-tower] gives a tower dominating both, so it suffices to compare a triangle indexed 1 refining a triangle indexed 2. Write $h:\overline X_1\to\overline X_2$, $k:\overline Y_1\to\overline Y_2$, $h':V_1\to V_2$, and $q_1=q_2k$. Set $P_i=Rp_{i*}$, $L_i=Rp_{Yi*}$, $H=Rh_*$, $H'=Rh'_*$, $M=Rk_*$, $J_i=c_{i!}$, $B_i=b_{i!}$ and $I_i=v_{i!}$. Step 3 identifies $P_2H=MP_1$ and $L_2H'=L_1$. The squares A (top $X\hookrightarrow V_1$, bottom $X\hookrightarrow V_2$, vertical $\operatorname{id}_X,h'$), D (top $Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y_1$, bottom $Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y_2$, vertical $\operatorname{id}_Y,k$), and E (top $X\hookrightarrow\overline X_1$, bottom $X\hookrightarrow\overline X_2$, vertical $\operatorname{id}_X,h$) yield $\gamma_A:J_2\to H'J_1$, $\gamma_D:I_2\to MI_1$ and $\gamma_E:B_2J_2\to HB_1J_1$. By the normalization in [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence], these are precisely the alpha comparisons of [def-weil-pbc-proper-open-comparison]. The Cartesian model squares B and C for indices 2 and 1 yield $\gamma_B:I_2L_2\to P_2B_2$ and $\gamma_C:I_1L_1\to P_1B_1$. The square F with top $V_1\hookrightarrow\overline X_1$, bottom $V_2\hookrightarrow\overline X_2$, vertical $h',h$ yields $\gamma_F:B_2H'\to HB_1$. Horizontal and vertical pasting [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] give
$$\gamma_E=(\gamma_FJ_1)\circ(B_2\gamma_A),\qquad (M\gamma_C)\circ(\gamma_DL_1)=(P_2\gamma_F)\circ(\gamma_BH').$$
Naturality of $\gamma_B$ at $\gamma_{A,K}:J_2K\to H'J_1K$ gives
$$(P_2B_2\gamma_A)\circ(\gamma_BJ_2)=(\gamma_BH'J_1)\circ(I_2L_2\gamma_A).$$
Substitution gives the fully whiskered equality
$$(P_2\gamma_E)\circ(\gamma_BJ_2)=(M\gamma_CJ_1)\circ(\gamma_DL_1J_1)\circ(I_2L_2\gamma_A).$$
Apply $Rq_{2*}$. The pushforward identifications and their coherence from step 3 and the open-extension identifications [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] identify this equality with the commuting square between the two model composition maps and the three refinement comparisons. Choice-independent cocycles [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-compactification-independence] then cancel the comparisons through the dominating triangle and prove independence of all auxiliary choices.

proof.text:
For $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}S\xrightarrow{h}T$, choose successive compactifications $S\xhookrightarrow{w}\overline S\xrightarrow{r}T$, $Y\xhookrightarrow{v}\overline Y\xrightarrow{q}\overline S$ of $wg$, and $X\xhookrightarrow{a}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}\overline Y$ of $vf$, by [lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle]. The ambient schemes are Noetherian and qcqs by the step-1 calculation applied to each proper map. Put $W=\overline Y\times_{\overline S}S$, $V=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}W$, and $U=\overline X\times_{\overline Y}Y$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Denote the open inclusions by $d:Y\hookrightarrow W$, $i:W\hookrightarrow\overline Y$, $c:U\hookrightarrow V$, $b:V\hookrightarrow\overline X$, and $j:X\hookrightarrow U$, with $id=v$ and $bcj=a$; write the proper projections as $q_S:W\to S$, $p_W:V\to W$ and $p_Y:U\to Y$. These are successive restrictions in the cited compatible-triangle construction. The adjacent Cartesian squares are A (top $U\xrightarrow{c}V$, bottom $Y\xrightarrow{d}W$, vertical $p_Y,p_W$), B (top $V\xrightarrow{b}\overline X$, bottom $W\xrightarrow{i}\overline Y$, vertical $p_W,p$), and C (top $W\xrightarrow{i}\overline Y$, bottom $S\xrightarrow{w}\overline S$, vertical $q_S,q$). Their maps are
$$\gamma_A:d_!Rp_{Y*}\to Rp_{W*}c_!,\quad \gamma_B:i_!Rp_{W*}\to Rp_*b_!,\quad \gamma_C:w_!Rq_{S*}\to Rq_*i_!.$$
Step 4 permits both parenthesizations to be computed on these models. Starting from $Rr_*w_!Rq_{S*}d_!Rp_{Y*}j_!$, one route uses A then the vertically pasted rectangle B+C; the other uses C then the horizontally pasted rectangle A+B. The pasting formulas [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] are
$$\gamma_{A+B}=(\gamma_Bc_!)\circ(i_!\gamma_A),\qquad \gamma_{B+C}=(Rq_*\gamma_B)\circ(\gamma_CRp_{W*}).$$
The middle transformations commute by the explicit naturality identity
$$(\gamma_CRp_{W*}c_!)\circ(w_!Rq_{S*}\gamma_A)=(Rq_*i_!\gamma_A)\circ(\gamma_Cd_!Rp_{Y*}),$$
checked at each object by naturality of $\gamma_C$ at $\gamma_{A,K}$. Whisker by $Rr_*$ and $j_!$ and compose with $Rq_*\gamma_Bc_!$. Both routes are now the same map to $Rr_*Rq_*Rp_*b_!c_!j_!$. The associative direct-image identifications from step 3 and the coherent open-extension composition [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition] identify this target with $R(rqp)_*a_!$. Finally the choice-independent cocycles [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-compactification-independence] conjugate this equality to the original candidates, proving associativity.
